html:
The ruler of the Huns from 434 until his death in 453, at first with his brother Bleda, whom he probably had killed around 445. From the Hungarian plain he ruled a Hunnic empire of Huns, Goths, Gepids and other peoples. Christian writers called him the Scourge of God.

The Huns had crossed into Europe around 370 and set off the great migrations. Attila raided the Balkan lands of the Eastern Empire again and again and forced Theodosius II to pay heavy tribute in gold. In 451 he invaded Gaul and was checked by the Roman general Aetius and the Visigoths at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains. In 452 he invaded Italy and sacked Aquileia, then turned back after meeting Pope Leo I, perhaps also because of disease and hunger in his army.

He died on his wedding night in 453, apparently of a burst blood vessel. His empire fell apart within a few years, and the peoples it had held went their own way.
